title: Fixed Removable Deckle and Laid Wire Paper Mould
description: One newly authored whole hand-papermaking mould-and-matching-deckle instrument in a fixed separated resting pose. One continuous rectangular timber mould frame carries six complete underside ribs, six whole round transverse chain wires and forty-one separate complete longitudinal laid wires. Actual empty cells remain between wires; no opaque substitute sheet, transparency texture or watermark drawing is used. Its one complete removable deckle rests beside it, rotated slightly in plan; a continuous underside recess and upper inward lip are genuine solid geometry around the entire open centre. Both matching pieces rest on finite flat bottom surfaces. All numerical geometry newly authored; no press platen, hinge, suspension stand, pull handle or old seed-sieve lattice imported. The paired mould and its subordinate fitted rim are one complete tool, not two new independent models or a scene. Four opaque PBR appearances, metres and native Z up. Static stylized visual only; wire spacing is deliberately coarse for legibility, not a historical reconstruction, mesh specification, fit certification, drainage, papermaking quality, manufacturing or safety claim. No pulp, vat, finished paper, text, animation, rig or interaction.
